Multi-Cause Mortality Forecasting and Reconciliation

Source: vignettes/multi-cause-forecasting.Rmd
multi-cause-forecasting.Rmd

Overview

When forecasting mortality by cause of death, a key challenge is coherence: disease-specific forecasts should sum to the all-cause forecast at every age, year, and population group. mortensor provides two strategies:

  1. Post-hoc reconciliation (reconcile(), run_reconciled_forecast()): Forecast each cause independently, then adjust via weighted least squares (WLS) so that diseases sum to all-cause
  2. Compositional coherence (run_coherent_forecast()): Model cause shares jointly using Tucker4-ILR, ensuring coherence by construction

This vignette covers both approaches end-to-end.

Data requirements

Multi-cause forecasting requires:

  • A mort_data object for each cause with the same age groups, years, and population strata
  • A mort_data object for all-cause mortality
  • Cause-specific rates should sum to approximately (but not necessarily exactly) the all-cause rate
library(mortensor)

# Example: three causes + all-cause
# (In practice, use read_mortality() or the ONS pipeline)
data_cancer  <- mort_data(mx_cancer, ages, years, groups, cause = "Cancer")
data_cvd     <- mort_data(mx_cvd,    ages, years, groups, cause = "CVD")
data_resp    <- mort_data(mx_resp,   ages, years, groups, cause = "Respiratory")
data_all     <- mort_data(mx_all,    ages, years, groups, cause = "All causes")

Strategy 1: Independent forecasts + WLS reconciliation

Step-by-step workflow

1. Forecast each cause independently 

# Smooth and calibrate each cause
sm_cancer <- smooth_mortality(data_cancer, method = "gam",
                              covid_years = c(2020L, 2021L))
sm_cvd    <- smooth_mortality(data_cvd, method = "gam",
                              covid_years = c(2020L, 2021L))
sm_resp   <- smooth_mortality(data_resp, method = "gam",
                              covid_years = c(2020L, 2021L))
sm_all    <- smooth_mortality(data_all, method = "gam",
                              covid_years = c(2020L, 2021L))

# Calibrate and forecast each
cal_cancer <- calibrate(sm_cancer, holdout_frac = 0.2, ensemble = TRUE)
cal_cvd    <- calibrate(sm_cvd,    holdout_frac = 0.2, ensemble = TRUE)
cal_resp   <- calibrate(sm_resp,   holdout_frac = 0.2, ensemble = TRUE)
cal_all    <- calibrate(sm_all,    holdout_frac = 0.2, ensemble = TRUE)

fc_cancer <- forecast(cal_cancer, h = 10)
fc_cvd    <- forecast(cal_cvd,    h = 10)
fc_resp   <- forecast(cal_resp,   h = 10)
fc_all    <- forecast(cal_all,    h = 10)

# Add prediction intervals
fc_cancer <- add_pi(fc_cancer, n_sim = 500, method = "bootstrap")
fc_cvd    <- add_pi(fc_cvd,    n_sim = 500, method = "bootstrap")
fc_resp   <- add_pi(fc_resp,   n_sim = 500, method = "bootstrap")

2. Reconcile 

recon <- reconcile(
  forecasts = list(
    cancer = fc_cancer,
    cvd    = fc_cvd,
    resp   = fc_resp
  ),
  all_cause = fc_all
)

The reconcile() function returns a named list of adjusted mort_forecast objects. Each disease forecast is modified so that:

mx,t,gcancer+mx,t,gcvd+mx,t,gresp+mx,t,gresidual=mx,t,gall m^{\text{cancer}}_{x,t,g} + m^{\text{cvd}}_{x,t,g} + m^{\text{resp}}_{x,t,g} + m^{\text{residual}}_{x,t,g} = m^{\text{all}}_{x,t,g}

3. Use reconciled forecasts 

# All standard methods work on reconciled forecasts
plot(recon$cancer, type = "trends")
summary(recon$cvd)
export(recon$resp, dir = "results/")
le_cancer <- life_expectancy(recon$cancer)

WLS reconciliation: how it works

The WLS reconciliation solves:

𝐦̂=𝐒(𝐒⊤𝐖−1𝐒)−1𝐒⊤𝐖−1𝐦̃ \hat{\mathbf{m}} = \mathbf{S} (\mathbf{S}^\top \mathbf{W}^{-1} \mathbf{S})^{-1} \mathbf{S}^\top \mathbf{W}^{-1} \tilde{\mathbf{m}}

where:

  • 𝐦̃\tilde{\mathbf{m}} is the stacked vector of independent disease forecasts plus the all-cause forecast
  • 𝐒\mathbf{S} is the summing matrix enforcing mall=∑kmkm_{\text{all}} = \sum_k m_k
  • 𝐖\mathbf{W} is a diagonal weight matrix based on in-sample forecast variance (inverse variance weighting)

This gives the minimum-variance linear unbiased adjustment to the independent forecasts.

wls_reconcile() directly

For lower-level control:

recon_raw <- wls_reconcile(
  mx_all_fc    = fc_all$mx_point,                         # 3D array
  mx_indep     = list(cancer = fc_cancer$mx_point,        # named list of 3D arrays
                      cvd    = fc_cvd$mx_point,
                      resp   = fc_resp$mx_point),
  bs_indep     = list(cancer = list(mx_lower = fc_cancer$mx_lower,
                                    mx_upper = fc_cancer$mx_upper,
                                    mx_median = fc_cancer$mx_median),
                      cvd    = list(mx_lower = fc_cvd$mx_lower,
                                    mx_upper = fc_cvd$mx_upper,
                                    mx_median = fc_cvd$mx_median),
                      resp   = list(mx_lower = fc_resp$mx_lower,
                                    mx_upper = fc_resp$mx_upper,
                                    mx_median = fc_resp$mx_median)),
  disease_order = c("cancer", "cvd", "resp"),
  recon_cap     = 0.5              # max adjustment as fraction of point forecast
)

# Result:
# recon_raw$mx_recon  — named list of reconciled 3D point forecast arrays
# recon_raw$bs_recon  — named list of reconciled PI bounds
# recon_raw$delta     — adjustment applied (for diagnostics)
# recon_raw$sigma_sq  — estimated variance per disease

The recon_cap parameter

To prevent extreme adjustments (which can arise when disease shares are small), the recon_cap limits the absolute adjustment to a fraction of the point forecast:

|δk|≤recon_cap×mkindep|\delta_k| \leq \text{recon\_cap} \times m^{\text{indep}}_k

The default recon_cap = 0.5 allows adjustments of up to 50% of the original forecast. Lower values produce more conservative reconciliation.

Enforcing additional constraints 

# Enforce that disease rates don't exceed all-cause (hard cap)
fc_capped <- enforce_coherence(
  disease_fc_list = list(cancer = fc_cancer$mx_point,
                         cvd    = fc_cvd$mx_point),
  all_cause_fc    = fc_all$mx_point
)

# Correct for population structure mismatches between group averages
fc_corrected <- correct_group_means(
  disease_fc = fc_cancer$mx_point,
  pop_array  = sm_all$pop
)

Strategy 2: Tucker4-ILR coherent forecasting

Concept

Instead of forecasting each cause independently and reconciling post-hoc, the Tucker4-ILR approach models the cause-specific structure jointly:

  1. Compute disease shares: sx,t,g,k=mx,t,g,k/mx,t,g,alls_{x,t,g,k} = m_{x,t,g,k} / m_{x,t,g,\text{all}}
  2. Apply ILR transform (maps the K+1K+1 simplex to ℝK\mathbb{R}^K)
  3. Fit Tucker4 on the 4D ILR tensor
  4. Forecast the B-mode (time dimension)
  5. Invert ILR to recover coherent shares
  6. Multiply by all-cause forecast to get rates

This guarantees ∑ksk=1\sum_k s_k = 1 at every (x,t,g)(x, t, g) by construction.

Step-by-step 

# 1. Compute shares
shares_4d <- compute_cause_shares(
  mx_disease_list = list(cancer = data_cancer$mx,
                         cvd    = data_cvd$mx,
                         resp   = data_resp$mx),
  mx_all          = data_all$mx,
  disease_order   = c("cancer", "cvd", "resp")
)
# Result: [n_ages x n_years x n_groups x 4]
# The 4th element is the residual (1 - cancer - cvd - resp)

# 2. ILR transform
X_ilr <- ilr_cause_transform(shares_4d)
# Result: [n_ages x n_years x n_groups x 3]

# 3. Calibrate Tucker4 ranks
calib_t4 <- calibrate_tucker4(
  X_ilr           = X_ilr,
  mx_all          = data_all$mx,
  mx_disease_list = list(cancer = data_cancer$mx,
                         cvd    = data_cvd$mx,
                         resp   = data_resp$mx),
  disease_order   = c("cancer", "cvd", "resp"),
  years           = data_all$years,
  h_val           = 3,
  min_train       = 12
)

# 4. Forecast
fc_t4 <- tucker4_coherent_forecast(
  X_ilr       = X_ilr,
  years       = data_all$years,
  h           = 10,
  R_A         = calib_t4$R_A,
  R_B         = calib_t4$R_B,
  R_C         = calib_t4$R_C,
  R_D         = calib_t4$R_D,
  ts_method   = calib_t4$ts_method,
  return_full = TRUE
)

# 5. Verify coherence
all(abs(apply(fc_t4$shares_forecast, c(1,2,3), sum) - 1) < 1e-10)
# TRUE — shares sum to 1 everywhere

# 6. Recover disease-specific rates
fc_all_point <- forecast(cal_all, h = 10)$mx_point
mx_cancer_fc <- fc_t4$shares_forecast[, , , 1] * fc_all_point
mx_cvd_fc    <- fc_t4$shares_forecast[, , , 2] * fc_all_point
mx_resp_fc   <- fc_t4$shares_forecast[, , , 3] * fc_all_point

Bootstrap for Tucker4 

bs_t4 <- bootstrap_coherent_forecast(
  fc_obj     = fc_t4,
  mx_all_fc  = fc_all_point,
  n_sim      = 500,
  h          = 10
)

# bs_t4$mx_lower, $mx_upper, $mx_median: 4D arrays [n_a x h x n_g x K]

Visualise share evolution 

plot_share_evolution(
  shares_obs_4d = shares_4d,
  shares_fc_4d  = fc_t4$shares_forecast,
  years_obs     = data_all$years,
  years_fc      = 2021:2030,
  disease_order = c("cancer", "cvd", "resp", "residual"),
  output_dir    = tempdir(),
  group_index   = 1,
  groups        = data_all$groups
)

Pipeline functions

For batch processing, use the monolithic pipeline functions:

run_reconciled_forecast() 

shared <- mort_shared_config(
  output_dir  = "results/reconciled/",
  forecast_h  = 10,
  n_sim       = 500,
  seed        = 42
)

disease_configs <- list(
  cancer = mort_config(cause_label = "Cancer",      cause_short = "cancer"),
  cvd    = mort_config(cause_label = "CVD",         cause_short = "cvd"),
  resp   = mort_config(cause_label = "Respiratory", cause_short = "resp")
)

ac_config <- mort_config(cause_label = "All causes", cause_short = "all")

result <- run_reconciled_forecast(disease_configs, ac_config, shared)

# result is a named list of mort_forecast objects (one per disease + all-cause)
names(result)
# [1] "cancer" "cvd" "resp" "all"

# Each is a full mort_forecast with PIs and disaggregation
plot(result$cancer, type = "trends")
life_expectancy(result$cvd)

run_coherent_forecast() 

shared <- mort_shared_config(
  output_dir = "results/coherent/",
  forecast_h = 10,
  n_sim      = 500,
  seed       = 42
)

result <- run_coherent_forecast(disease_configs, ac_config, shared)

Comparing reconciliation strategies

Feature WLS Reconciliation Tucker4-ILR
Coherence Post-hoc adjustment By construction
Model flexibility Any model per cause Joint Tucker4 for all causes
Cause interactions Not modelled Captured via 4th mode
Speed Fast (linear algebra) Moderate (4D Tucker)
Bootstrap Per-cause, then reconcile Joint coherent bootstrap
When to use Many causes, diverse patterns Few causes, structured shares

Practical guidance

  • For 10+ diseases with diverse age patterns, WLS reconciliation with per-cause ensemble models is more flexible
  • For 2–5 major cause groups where share dynamics are the primary interest (e.g. cancer vs CVD vs other), Tucker4-ILR is more principled
  • Both can be run and compared using proper scoring rules (see the scoring-and-evaluation vignette)

Consistency diagnostics

Check that diseases sum to all-cause 

# After reconciliation, verify the sum constraint
plot_consistency_check(
  fc_dt_combined = rbind(
    to_data_table(recon$cancer)[, cause := "cancer"],
    to_data_table(recon$cvd)[, cause := "cvd"],
    to_data_table(recon$resp)[, cause := "resp"]
  ),
  ac_fc_dt  = to_data_table(fc_all),
  output_dir = tempdir()
)

This produces a boxplot of ∑kmk/mall\sum_k m_k / m_{\text{all}} across ages, years, and groups. After WLS reconciliation, this ratio should be very close to 1. After Tucker4-ILR, it is exactly 1.

Default disease configurations

For UK ONS data, default_disease_order() and default_configs() provide pre-built configurations for the 10 major cause groups:

# Standard UK disease ordering
default_disease_order()
# [1] "ihd" "cancer" "dementia" "stroke" "copd"
# [6] "cvd_other" "diabetes" "liver" "alc_suicide" "residual"

# Pre-configured mort_config objects for each
configs <- default_configs()
names(configs)
# [1] "all" "ihd" "cancer" "dementia" "stroke" "copd"
# [7] "cvd_other" "diabetes" "liver" "alc_suicide" "residual"

# Use with pipeline
shared <- mort_shared_config(output_dir = "results/")
disease_cfgs <- configs[setdiff(names(configs), "all")]
result <- run_reconciled_forecast(disease_cfgs, configs$all, shared)

Complete example 

library(mortensor)

# --- Setup data (assuming mort_data objects exist) ---
diseases <- list(cancer = data_cancer, cvd = data_cvd, resp = data_resp)
ac_data  <- data_all

# --- Strategy 1: Independent + Reconcile ---
forecasts <- lapply(diseases, function(d) {
  sm  <- smooth_mortality(d, method = "gam", covid_years = c(2020L, 2021L))
  cal <- calibrate(sm, holdout_frac = 0.2, ensemble = TRUE)
  fc  <- forecast(cal, h = 10)
  add_pi(fc, n_sim = 500, method = "bootstrap")
})

sm_all  <- smooth_mortality(ac_data, method = "gam",
                            covid_years = c(2020L, 2021L))
cal_all <- calibrate(sm_all, holdout_frac = 0.2, ensemble = TRUE)
fc_all  <- forecast(cal_all, h = 10)

recon <- reconcile(forecasts, all_cause = fc_all)

# --- Strategy 2: Tucker4-ILR ---
shares <- compute_cause_shares(
  lapply(diseases, `[[`, "mx"), ac_data$mx,
  disease_order = names(diseases)
)
X_ilr   <- ilr_cause_transform(shares)
calib4  <- calibrate_tucker4(X_ilr, ac_data$mx,
                             lapply(diseases, `[[`, "mx"),
                             names(diseases), ac_data$years)
fc4     <- tucker4_coherent_forecast(X_ilr, ac_data$years, h = 10,
                                     R_A = calib4$R_A, R_B = calib4$R_B,
                                     R_C = calib4$R_C, R_D = calib4$R_D,
                                     ts_method = calib4$ts_method)

# --- Compare strategies ---
# Both produce cause-specific forecasts; evaluate with scoring rules
